questions.title: Territory of the inferior mesenteric artery
questions.question: The inferior mesenteric artery supplies blood to:

options.B: The small intestine and ascending colon
options.C: The transverse and descending colon, sigmoid colon, and rectum

explanations.A: Incorrect. The stomach and spleen are foregut-related and are supplied by branches of the coeliac trunk (left gastric, splenic and short gastric arteries), not the inferior mesenteric artery.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The small intestine and ascending colon are midgut derivatives supplied by the superior mesenteric artery, not the inferior mesenteric artery.
explanations.C: Correct. The inferior mesenteric artery is the artery of the hindgut, supplying the distal (left) third of the transverse colon, the descending and sigmoid colon and the upper rectum through its left colic, sigmoid and superior rectal branches. Its territory begins near the splenic flexure, the watershed zone of Griffiths, where it meets the superior mesenteric supply. The proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon remain superior mesenteric (midgut) territory.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The liver, gallbladder and pancreas are foregut derivatives supplied from the coeliac trunk (via the hepatic and splenic arteries), with the pancreatic head also receiving superior mesenteric supply.

questions.learning_objective: State the colonic and rectal territory supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery.

questions.title: Branches of the common hepatic artery
questions.question: The common hepatic artery, a branch of the coeliac trunk, gives rise to which of the following arteries?

options.A: Left gastric and right gastric arteries
options.B: Proper hepatic and left gastric arteries

explanations.A: Incorrect. The left gastric artery is a separate direct branch of the coeliac trunk, not a branch of the common hepatic artery.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The common hepatic artery continues as the hepatic artery proper after giving off the gastroduodenal artery; the proper hepatic artery is its continuation, not a co-branch alongside the left gastric.
explanations.C: Correct. The common hepatic artery runs to the right along the upper border of the pancreas and divides into the gastroduodenal artery, which descends behind the first part of the duodenum, and the hepatic artery proper, which continues to the liver in the free edge of the lesser omentum. The right gastric artery arises from the hepatic artery proper (or occasionally the common hepatic artery) and runs along the lesser curvature to anastomose with the left gastric artery. Thus the right gastric and gastroduodenal arteries are the vessels derived from this stem.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The splenic and left gastric arteries are the other two direct branches of the coeliac trunk itself, not branches of the common hepatic artery.

questions.subtopic: Coeliac trunk and stomach blood supply
questions.learning_objective: List the gastroduodenal and right gastric arteries as vessels derived from the common hepatic artery.

questions.title: Artery whose occlusion causes appendicular gangrene
questions.question: Gangrene of the appendix is due to occlusion of which artery?

explanations.A: Correct. The appendix is supplied by the appendicular artery, a branch of the ileocolic artery (itself a branch of the superior mesenteric artery), which runs to the appendix in the free edge of the mesoappendix. The appendicular artery is an end artery with no effective anastomosis, so thrombosis of it during appendicitis rapidly produces ischaemia and gangrene of the appendix. Occlusion of the parent ileocolic artery similarly cuts off this sole supply.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The middle colic artery supplies the transverse colon, well away from the appendix.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The right colic artery supplies the ascending colon, not the appendix.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The left colic artery is a branch of the inferior mesenteric artery supplying the descending colon and has no relation to the appendix.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the appendicular artery (from the ileocolic artery) as the end artery whose occlusion causes appendicular gangrene.

questions.title: Shape of the right suprarenal gland
questions.question: Regarding the right suprarenal gland, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.B: It reaches the hilum of the kidney
options.C: It is related anteriorly to the stomach

explanations.A: Correct. The right suprarenal (adrenal) gland is pyramidal or triangular in shape and caps the upper pole of the right kidney, whereas the left gland is more elongated and semilunar (crescentic). It lies behind the inferior vena cava anteriorly and against the diaphragm and bare area of the liver. Its hilum, where the suprarenal vein leaves to drain directly into the inferior vena cava, faces anteromedially.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The suprarenal gland sits on the upper pole of the kidney and does not reach the renal hilum, which lies at the medial border of the kidney lower down.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The right suprarenal gland is related anteriorly to the inferior vena cava and the bare area of the liver, not to the stomach; the stomach relates to the left gland's region.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The hilum of the suprarenal gland faces anteromedially (transmitting the suprarenal vein), not downwards.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the pyramidal shape of the right suprarenal gland and its relation to the inferior vena cava.

questions.title: Development of the greater curvature of the stomach
questions.question: Regarding the development of the stomach, mark the one correct statement:

options.A: It is derived partly from foregut and partly from midgut
options.B: After rotation of 90 degrees around its anteroposterior axis, its right surface becomes posterior and its left surface anterior
options.C: Its rotation around its longitudinal axis forms the greater sac
options.D: The original posterior border of the stomach becomes the greater curvature after its rapid growth

explanations.A: Incorrect. The stomach develops entirely from the foregut; the foregut-midgut junction lies distally, at the level of the major duodenal papilla in the second part of the duodenum.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The stomach rotates 90 degrees clockwise around its longitudinal (craniocaudal) axis, so its left surface becomes anterior and its right surface posterior; the anteroposterior-axis rotation is a separate, lesser movement.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Rotation of the stomach and the growth of its dorsal mesogastrium create the lesser sac (omental bursa) behind the stomach, not the greater sac.
explanations.D: Correct. The dorsal (originally posterior) border of the developing stomach grows much faster than the ventral border, and this differential growth balloons it out to form the greater curvature. The slower-growing ventral border becomes the lesser curvature. The accompanying 90-degree clockwise rotation about the longitudinal axis then carries the greater curvature to the left and the lesser curvature to the right, and pulls the dorsal mesogastrium out to form the greater omentum.

questions.title: Formation of the main pancreatic duct
questions.question: The main pancreatic duct (of Wirsung) is formed by:

options.C: The whole dorsal pancreatic duct and the whole ventral pancreatic duct
options.D: The distal part of the dorsal pancreatic duct and the duct of the ventral pancreas

explanations.A: Incorrect. The proximal part of the dorsal duct usually persists only as the small accessory duct (of Santorini); the dorsal duct alone does not form the main duct.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The ventral duct forms only the distal, downstream part of the main duct near the ampulla; it cannot account for the whole main pancreatic duct.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The proximal part of the dorsal duct does not contribute to the main duct; it either disappears or remains as the accessory duct, so not the whole dorsal duct is included.
explanations.D: Correct. As the ventral and dorsal pancreatic buds fuse, their duct systems anastomose. The main pancreatic duct (of Wirsung) is formed by the entire ventral pancreatic duct together with the distal part of the dorsal pancreatic duct, and it opens with the bile duct at the major duodenal papilla. The proximal part of the dorsal duct persists as the accessory duct of Santorini, draining into the minor duodenal papilla.

questions.title: Derivative of the ureteric bud
questions.question: Which of the following structures is derived from the ureteric bud?

explanations.A: Correct. The ureteric bud, an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct, gives rise to the collecting system of the kidney: the ureter, renal pelvis, major and minor calyces, and the collecting tubules and ducts. Its repeated branching lays down this drainage tree. The nephron proper, by contrast, forms from the surrounding metanephric mesenchyme (metanephric blastema).
explanations.B: Incorrect. Bowman's capsule is part of the nephron and develops from the metanephric mesenchyme, not the ureteric bud.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The distal convoluted tubule is a nephron segment derived from the metanephric mesenchyme.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The proximal convoluted tubule is also a nephron segment formed from the metanephric mesenchyme.

questions.title: Male derivative of the mesonephric duct
questions.question: Which of the following structures develops from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct in the male?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The paradidymis is a remnant of mesonephric (excretory) tubules, not of the mesonephric duct itself.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The efferent ductules (vasa efferentia) develop from persisting mesonephric tubules that link the rete testis to the duct, not from the mesonephric duct.
explanations.C: Correct. In the male the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct persists under the influence of testosterone and gives rise to the epididymis, the ductus (vas) deferens, the ejaculatory duct and the seminal vesicle, which buds from its lower end. The seminal vesicle is therefore a direct outgrowth of the mesonephric duct. The paramesonephric (Mullerian) duct instead regresses, leaving only small remnants.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic utricle is the male remnant of the fused paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts, not a mesonephric-duct derivative.

questions.title: Derivative of the hindgut
questions.question: The hindgut gives rise to which of the following structures?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The ascending colon is a midgut derivative supplied by the superior mesenteric artery.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The gall bladder is a foregut derivative, arising as part of the hepatic diverticulum.
explanations.C: Correct. The hindgut gives rise to the distal (left) third of the transverse colon, the descending colon, the sigmoid colon, the rectum and the upper part of the anal canal (down to the pectinate line). Consistent with this, these structures are supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery, the artery of the hindgut. The sigmoid colon is therefore a hindgut derivative.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The caecum, like the appendix and ascending colon, is a midgut derivative.
